hypothesis: Prospective venue-matched observation on BTC, ETH, SOL, and HYPE can determine whether the exact HYPE breakout-onset rule produces repeatable signal paths outside HYPE without granting order authority or relying on historical transfer results alone.
decision: Run the four-asset, both-direction observer at 60-second cadence with an empty execution scope. Preserve all evaluations, blockers, and signal paths; do not route orders, infer executable profitability from counterfactual outcomes, or promote any mapping automatically. The older BTC/HYPE-only observer is retired because its coverage is a strict subset and duplicated public requests.
falsifier: Missing or duplicate mappings, cadence gaps, future decisions, any observer order or fill, non-none execution authority, correlated live rate-limit faults, or a changed profile fingerprint invalidates operational evidence. Repeated negative prospective after-cost paths reject transfer; repeatable positive paths across market states would justify only a separately frozen execution-friction challenger.
limitations: The new run initially contains one complete cycle and no eligible signal, so it provides operational evidence only.
Historical transfer evidence rejects unchanged ETH and SOL and shows a development-to-holdout sign reversal for BTC shorts.
Observer counterfactual paths cannot reproduce IOC acknowledgement latency, private queue position, or realized fill slippage.
The current HYPE live lifecycle and active profile were not changed or restarted.
The observer adds four public-data evaluations per minute; continued live fault and cadence monitoring is required.
